target_customer: Staffing companies, labor marketplaces and workforce platforms that need embedded onboarding, payroll and billing
problem: Platforms paying many hourly workers cannot find payroll infrastructure with daily pay and flexible earnings. Zeal sells that as an API.
business_model: B2B API and SaaS payroll infrastructure with usage fees

founders.name: Pranab Krishnan
founders.background_notes: Sources: YC page, Zeal about page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Payroll needs tax filing across states, compliance and money movement integrations, hard for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Payroll compliance, SOC 2 and deep customer integrations create switching costs; the API idea itself is replicable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Gusto launched an embedded payroll API in 2021-06, after the batch. The company reached a Series B in 2024 while repositioning for staffing firms.

market_need_then: The founders themselves had to move thousands of 1099 contractors to W-2 and could not find payroll tools with daily pay and customizable earnings, which is the pain that led to the product.

branding.domain_note: Uses zeal.com; legal entity still Puzzl Group Inc.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission: ensure every American worker gets paid correctly, on time, and without friction

rebrands.why: Not stated; Dealroom says the rename coincided with the Series A

brand_strength.rationale: A clean, short name but no press about the brand itself; a B2B infrastructure brand sold on product.

pivots.from: Puzzl, payment processing and staffing for the gig economy
pivots.why: Regulation forced reclassification of 1099 contractors to W-2 and no payroll provider met their needs (Zeal about page).

outcome_analysis: Zeal started as Puzzl, a gig economy staffing and payment startup in YC Summer 2019. After reclassifying contractors to W-2 it built a payroll API, raising a $1.6M seed in 2020, a $13M Series A led by Spark Capital in 2021, and a $15M Series B led by Portage in 2024. It is active with about 45 people and has repositioned toward staffing firms. The pivot found a market, though competition from Check and Gusto grew after founding.
notes: Series A was also reported by BusinessWire and others (BusinessWire page returned 403); Zeal's about page says the Series B was 2023 while BusinessWire dates it 2024-10-10, the press release date is used. Dealroom snippet lists a $150K pre-seed in 2019, unverified and not recorded. Competitors: no source dated near the 2019 batch was found for gig payments competitors; TechCrunch 2021 names ADP and Paycor as processors the founders looked at, and Check (embedded payroll) and Gusto Embedded (2021-06) came later, so the list is empty. Founders' education and prior employers were not found.
